Car Battery Dead How to Start || Easily Identify Vehicle Battery Draining Problem

Car Battery Dead

If your car battery is dead, you will need to jump start it. You will need to connect one of the jumper cables to the positive terminal of the dead battery, then the other end of the cable to the positive terminal of the good battery. Then, connect one of the other cables to the negative terminal of the good battery and the remaining cable to an unpainted metal surface on the car with the dead battery. Once the cables are connected, start the car with the good battery and let it run for a few minutes. Finally, try to start the car with the dead battery. If it starts, disconnect the cables in the reverse order as you connected them.

If your car's engine does not start, it may be due to one of the following fuses.

1.- If the general fuse is blown, there will be no power supply.

2.- When the fuel pump fuse fails, there is no fuel in the engine cylinders.

3.- If the fuse of the computer (ECU) is damaged then the engine will not start.

If your FAW V2 won’t start and makes no sound when you turn the key, here are the most common causes:
 1. Dead or Weak Battery
 • Headlights dim or don’t turn on.
 • Battery voltage below 12.4V.
 • Try jump-starting the car.
 2. Loose or Corroded Battery Terminals
 • Check and clean terminals.
 • Tighten battery connections properly.
 3. Faulty Ignition Switch
 • Key turns but starter doesn’t engage.
 • Try wiggling the key—if it occasionally starts, switch is failing.
 4. Blown Fuse or Bad Starter Relay
 • Check fuses related to ignition and starter in the fuse box.
 • Swap the starter relay with another similar one to test.
 5. Faulty Starter Motor or Solenoid
 • If no click at all → solenoid may be bad.
 • If one click but no crank → motor could be jammed or brushes worn.
 6. Ground Wire Problem
 • Check engine ground strap.
 • Rust or loose bolts can interrupt current flow to starter.
 7. Neutral Safety Switch (Automatic) / Clutch Switch (Manual)
 • Try starting in Neutral instead of Park.
 • For manual transmission, ensure clutch is fully pressed.

How does a car battery supply power to the starter motor, ignition system and alternator? 🔋🚗

This simplified wiring diagram shows:

🔴 High-current path: Battery → Starter Motor
🟡 Control path: Ignition Switch → Starter Solenoid
⚡ Charging path: Alternator B+ → Battery/Fuse Box
⚫ Ground: Battery, starter and alternator → Engine/Chassis

The starter solenoid uses a low-current control signal to switch the starter motor's high current.

⚠️ Actual vehicle wiring varies by make, model and electrical architecture. This is a simplified educational diagram.
